en.question: Should I take malaria drugs before getting tested?
en.answer: Always get a rapid diagnostic test or blood test at a clinic or pharmacy before starting malaria medicine. Not every fever is malaria, and testing ensures you receive the right care.
en.undiagnosed_text: If you have not been tested yet: do not start malaria tablets just by guessing. Always get a rapid diagnostic test (RDT) or blood smear at a clinic or pharmacy first, because many other fevers look like malaria. While going for the test, drink clean water and rest.
en.diagnosed_text: If a doctor or clinic has already tested and diagnosed malaria: start your prescribed artemisinin-based (ACT) tablets promptly with food or a fatty drink if advised, complete every tablet over the full 3 days, and return to the clinic if fever lasts beyond 48 hours or danger signs appear.

yo.question: Ṣé ó yẹ kí n lo oògùn ibà kí n tó ṣe àyẹ̀wò ẹ̀jẹ̀?
yo.answer: Máa ṣe àyẹ̀wò ibà RDT tàbí àyẹ̀wò ẹ̀jẹ̀ ní ilé ìwòsàn kí o tó bẹ̀rẹ̀ oògùn ibà. Kì í ṣe gbogbo ìgbóná ara ni ó jẹ́ malárìà, àyẹ̀wò sì ń jẹ́ kí o gba ìtọ́jú tó tọ́.
yo.undiagnosed_text: Tí o kò bá tíì ṣe àyẹ̀wò rárá: má ṣe lo oògùn ibà lásán láì ṣàyẹ̀wò. Lọ sí ilé ìwòsàn tàbí ilé oògùn láti ṣe àyẹ̀wò ẹ̀jẹ̀ RDT kókó, nítorí kì í ṣe gbogbo ìgbóná ara ló jẹ́ malárìà. Máa mu omi mímọ́ dáadáa kí o sì sinmi.
yo.diagnosed_text: Tí dókítà bá ti ṣàyẹ̀wò tí wọ́n sì ti fìdí ibà múlẹ̀ fún ọ: bẹ̀rẹ̀ lílo oògùn ibà ACT tí wọ́n kọ fún ọ kíákíá, parí gbogbo oògùn náà láti ọjọ́ kínní dé kẹta kódà bí ara rẹ bá ti yá, kí o sì padà sí ilé ìwòsàn bí ibà kò bá lọ sílẹ̀ lẹ́yìn ọjọ́ méjì.

en.question: Why must I finish all my malaria medicine even if I feel better?
en.answer: Finish every prescribed malaria tablet even after fever disappears. Stopping early leaves hidden parasites in your blood, causing the malaria to return and become harder to treat.
en.undiagnosed_text: If you have not been tested by a clinician yet: before buying or finishing antimalarial packs on your own, get tested first so you know whether fever is truly malaria or another infection that needs different care.
en.diagnosed_text: If a doctor diagnosed malaria and prescribed an ACT course: finish every single tablet on schedule even when fever disappears after day one. Stopping halfway leaves parasites in your blood, causing malaria to return stronger and harder to cure.

yo.question: Kí ló dé tí mo gbọ́dọ̀ parí oògùn ibà mi bí ara mi bá ti yá?
yo.answer: Parí gbogbo oògùn ibà tí wọ́n kọ fún ọ kódà nígbà tí ìgbóná ara bá ti lọ sílẹ̀. Dídáwọ́ rẹ̀ dúró kíákíá lè jẹ́ kí kòkòrò ibà ṣẹ́kù nínú ẹ̀jẹ̀, kí àrùn náà tún padà wá.
yo.undiagnosed_text: Tí dókítà kò bá tíì ṣàyẹ̀wò rẹ: kí o tó ra oògùn ibà fúnra rẹ, ṣe àyẹ̀wò ẹ̀jẹ̀ ní ilé ìwòsàn láti mọ̀ bóyá ibà gidi ni tàbí àìsàn mìíràn tí ó nílò ìtọ́jú ọ̀tọ̀.
yo.diagnosed_text: Tí dókítà bá ti fìdí ibà múlẹ̀ tí ó sì kọ oògùn ACT fún ọ: parí gbogbo oògùn náà ní àkókò rẹ̀ kódà nígbà tí ìgbóná ara bá ti lọ sílẹ̀. Dídáwọ́ rẹ̀ dúró lè jẹ́ kí kòkòrò ibà ṣẹ́kù nínú ẹ̀jẹ̀.

en.question: How can my family prevent malaria at home?
en.answer: Sleep every night under a treated mosquito net, clear standing water around your compound, and fit window screens to keep mosquitoes out.
en.undiagnosed_text: If you feel well and have not been diagnosed: protect your household every night by sleeping under an insecticide-treated mosquito net, draining stagnant puddles around your home, and fitting window screens. If anyone develops fever, test promptly.
en.diagnosed_text: If a family member is already diagnosed with malaria: continue sleeping under a treated net even while on treatment so mosquitoes do not carry the parasite from the sick person to other people in the home, and finish the prescribed course.

en.question: What should I do when someone starts having a fever and chills?
en.answer: Give plenty of clean drinking water, dress the person in light clothing, sponge with lukewarm water if uncomfortable, and visit the nearest health centre promptly for a check-up.
en.undiagnosed_text: If a person has fever and chills but has not seen a doctor yet: give plenty of clean drinking water, dress them in light clothes, sponge with lukewarm (not ice-cold) water, and take them to a health centre promptly for diagnosis rather than guessing medicines.
en.diagnosed_text: If a doctor has already diagnosed the cause of fever and given treatment: give prescribed medicines exactly on time, keep offering plenty of clean water and lukewarm sponging for comfort, and rush back to the clinic if convulsions, persistent vomiting, yellowing of eyes, or extreme weakness develops.

en.question: Can I have high blood pressure without feeling sick?
en.answer: Yes. High blood pressure often causes no obvious symptoms in the early stages, which is why regular blood pressure checks at a health centre or pharmacy are important for adults.
en.undiagnosed_text: If you have never had a high blood pressure diagnosis: remember high BP is often silent with no headache or pain. Have your blood pressure checked routinely at a primary health centre or licensed pharmacy, even when you feel healthy.
en.diagnosed_text: If a doctor has already diagnosed you with high blood pressure: never wait until you feel a headache or dizziness to check your BP or take your tablets—silent high BP damages the heart, brain, and kidneys over time when tablets are skipped.

yo.question: Ṣé ènìyàn lè ní ìfúnpá gíga láì rí àmì àìsàn kankan?

en.question: Can I stop taking my blood pressure medicine once my reading becomes normal?
en.answer: No. Your blood pressure stays normal because the medicine is working. Never stop or change prescribed blood pressure tablets without talking to your doctor or nurse.
en.undiagnosed_text: If you have not been diagnosed by a doctor: do not borrow someone else's blood pressure tablets if a single high reading shows up—get a proper clinical evaluation first so the doctor can confirm and pick a safe plan for you.
en.diagnosed_text: If a doctor diagnosed high blood pressure and prescribed daily tablets: keep taking your medicine every day even when your reading looks normal. Your BP is controlled because the tablets are working—never stop without speaking to your clinician.

en.question: What everyday diet habits help keep blood pressure steady?
en.answer: Cut down on table salt, seasoning cubes, and salty dried meats. Eat fresh vegetables, beans, and fruits daily, and walk briskly for 30 minutes most days.
en.undiagnosed_text: If you have not been diagnosed with high BP: keeping salt and seasoning cubes low, eating fresh vegetables, beans, and fruits daily, and walking briskly 30 minutes most days helps protect your blood pressure from rising.
en.diagnosed_text: If you are already diagnosed with high blood pressure: low-salt meals and regular brisk walking work alongside—not instead of—your prescribed BP medicine. Avoid salty dried meats, limit maggi cubes, and keep taking your tablets daily.

en.question: Is it safe to mix herbal agbo with prescribed blood pressure tablets?
en.answer: Be very careful: unmeasured herbal mixtures can clash with prescribed tablets or strain the kidneys and liver. Always tell your doctor before taking any herbal drink alongside hospital medicine.
en.undiagnosed_text: If you have not seen a doctor yet: do not use unlabelled herbal mixtures (agbo) to self-treat headaches or suspected high blood pressure—some contain hidden stimulants or strain the kidneys. Get a proper clinic BP check first.
en.diagnosed_text: If you are already taking prescribed blood pressure medicine: do not mix herbal agbo alongside your hospital tablets without telling your doctor, because herbal extracts can unpredictably crash your BP, block your tablets, or harm your kidneys and liver.

en.question: How do I prepare ORS for my child?
en.answer: Wash your hands with soap and water. Empty one full sachet of standard ORS into one litre of clean drinking water (check the sachet label), stir until completely dissolved, and discard any leftover mixture after 24 hours.
en.undiagnosed_text: If your child has loose stools and has not seen a doctor yet: start low-osmolarity ORS safely right away to prevent dehydration. Wash hands with soap, dissolve one whole standard ORS sachet in 1 litre of clean water (read the packet for exact volume), and seek clinic care promptly—especially if stools contain blood or fever is high.
en.diagnosed_text: If a health worker has already assessed your child and prescribed ORS plus zinc: prepare fresh ORS every 24 hours in 1 litre of clean drinking water as shown on the sachet, give sips after every loose stool, and continue daily zinc tablets for the full prescribed days.

en.question: Why do health workers give zinc together with ORS for child diarrhoea?
en.answer: Zinc tablets help shorten the duration and severity of diarrhoea episodes and strengthen the child's gut for the coming months when given for the full course advised by the clinic.
en.undiagnosed_text: If your child has not seen a health worker yet: start ORS immediately for hydration, and visit a clinic or pharmacy to get the age-appropriate zinc tablet dose—do not give adult tablets or leftovers to a young child.
en.diagnosed_text: If a health worker already prescribed zinc tablets alongside ORS: give one dose daily for the full 10 to 14 days advised, even if diarrhoea stops in two days. Zinc helps heal the gut lining and reduces future episodes.

en.question: Should I stop breastfeeding or feeding my child during diarrhoea?
en.answer: No. Continue breastfeeding more frequently and keep offering soft, nutritious meals alongside ORS so your child keeps strength and recovers faster.
en.undiagnosed_text: If your child has not been seen by a doctor yet: do not starve the child or stop breastmilk. Breastfeed more often alongside ORS, and go to a clinic urgently if the child refuses to suck, becomes very sleepy, or has blood in the stool.

en.question: When should a pregnant woman start antenatal clinic visits?
en.answer: Register for antenatal care as soon as you suspect or confirm you are pregnant. Early visits allow health workers to check your blood pressure, blood levels, and baby growth throughout pregnancy.
en.undiagnosed_text: If you think you might be pregnant and have not started antenatal care: visit a clinic promptly to confirm the pregnancy and begin antenatal checks—early visits check blood pressure, urine, blood count, and protect both mother and baby.
en.diagnosed_text: If your pregnancy is already confirmed and registered at antenatal clinic: attend every scheduled visit (even when feeling fine), bring your antenatal card, take routine clinic supplements as directed, and report any warning signs immediately.

yo.undiagnosed_text: Tí o bá fura pé o lóyún ṣùgbọ́n tí dókítà kò tíì ṣàyẹ̀wò rẹ: lọ sí ilé ìwòsàn kíákíá láti fìdí rẹ̀ múlẹ̀ kí o sì bẹ̀rẹ̀ ìforúkọsílẹ̀ aláboyún láti ṣàyẹ̀wò ìfúnpá, ìtọ̀, àti ẹ̀jẹ̀ rẹ ní àárọ̀.
yo.diagnosed_text: Tí dókítà bá ti fìdí oyún rẹ múlẹ̀ tí o sì ti bẹ̀rẹ̀ ìwòsàn aláboyún: máa lọ sí gbogbo ìpàdé ilé ìwòsàn rẹ déédéé, mú káàdì ìwòsàn rẹ dání, máa lo àwọn oògùn tí wọ́n fún ọ, kí o sì fi àmì ìkìlọ̀ tó dókítà létí lẹ́sẹ̀kẹsẹ̀.

en.question: Which warning signs in pregnancy need urgent clinic care?
en.answer: Go straight to a hospital or health centre if you notice any vaginal bleeding, severe headache with blurred vision, sudden swelling of your face or hands, high fever, or if your baby stops moving as usual.
en.undiagnosed_text: Whether you have registered for antenatal care yet or not: if you notice vaginal bleeding, severe headache with blurred vision, sudden hand/face swelling, high fever, severe belly pain, or fits in pregnancy, go to a hospital emergency unit right away.
en.diagnosed_text: Even if your antenatal checks were recently normal or you are already taking clinic tablets: danger signs like bleeding, blurred vision, severe headache, sudden swelling, water breaking early, or reduced baby kicks require immediate same-day hospital review.

en.question: What foods and routine clinic tablets support healthy blood levels in pregnancy?
en.answer: Antenatal clinics provide routine iron and folic acid tablets to protect mother and baby. Eating dark leafy vegetables, beans, eggs, fish, and fruits also supports strong blood.

en.question: How can I check if a medicine packet is genuine and not expired?
en.answer: Buy medicines only from licensed pharmacies or clinics. Check that the NAFDAC registration number is printed clearly, confirm the expiry date has not passed, inspect the unbroken seal, and avoid loose unlabelled tablets.
en.undiagnosed_text: Before buying any over-the-counter remedy when you have not seen a doctor: buy only from a licensed pharmacy or registered patent medicine shop, check the NAFDAC number, expiry date, and unbroken seal, and ask the pharmacist if a clinic check is safer first.
en.diagnosed_text: When picking up or taking medicine a doctor prescribed: double-check the NAFDAC number, expiry date, unbroken foil/bottle seal, and match the drug name and strength on the packet against your prescription before swallowing a dose.

en.question: Can I share leftover antibiotics or use them for another sickness?
en.answer: Never share antibiotics with anyone else or take leftover capsules for a new symptom. Wrong antibiotic use fails to cure the real cause of illness and breeds resistant infections.
en.undiagnosed_text: If you have not been diagnosed by a doctor: never swallow leftover antibiotics from a previous illness or someone else's pack—not every cough, fever, or stomach upset is bacterial, and wrong antibiotics waste time while building resistant germs.
en.diagnosed_text: If a doctor diagnosed a bacterial infection and prescribed antibiotics: take only the exact antibiotic prescribed for you, finish the full course even after feeling better, and do not save leftovers or share remaining capsules with family members.

en.question: Where should medicines be stored at home away from children?
en.answer: Keep medicines in their original labelled containers in a cool, dry place locked or high out of children's reach. Never pour liquid medicines into soft-drink bottles or leave pills in hot sunlight.
en.undiagnosed_text: Even for ordinary household remedies (like paracetamol or cough syrups) kept before a clinic visit: lock every bottle and blister pack up high in a cool, dry place in its original labelled container—never pour syrups into soft-drink bottles where children could drink them.
en.diagnosed_text: When storing prescribed family medicines during treatment: keep every child's and adult's prescribed bottles clearly separated in their original labelled boxes, away from sunlight and humidity, and locked high out of children's reach.

en.question: Why should I tell the pharmacist or doctor about all medicines I already take?
en.answer: Different brand-name medicines can contain the same active drug, such as paracetamol, or interact dangerously with one another. Sharing your current medicine list protects you from accidental double dosing.
en.undiagnosed_text: If you have not seen a doctor yet and are buying pharmacy medicines: tell the pharmacist everything you already took today (including painkillers, cold mixtures, and herbs) so you do not accidentally double-dose active drugs like paracetamol.
en.diagnosed_text: If you already take prescribed medicines (for example BP, diabetes, pregnancy, or malaria tablets): tell your doctor and pharmacist the full list before adding any new tablet, syrup, or herbal drink so treatments do not clash.
